name: In-context Learning with Retrieved Demonstrations for Language Models: A Survey (RetICL survey)
venue: TMLR 2024 (Transactions on Machine Learning Research). DBLP: journals/tmlr/0003XLPK24. Also arXiv:2401.11624 (submitted 21 Jan 2024, last revised v5 23 Mar 2024); subjects cs.CL/cs.AI/cs.IR.
authors_affiliation: Man Luo (Arizona State University; lead author), Xin Xu, Yue Liu, Panupong Pasupat, Mehran Kazemi (Google Research). Primary affiliations: Arizona State University and Google Research.
code_url: N/A (this is a survey; no method code repository is associated. No official accompanying code/repo found.)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (no continuously-updated paper list / leaderboard repo found for this survey) [uncertain]
task_domain: QA and broader NLP via in-context learning (ICL). The survey reviews retrieval-based ICL (RetICL) across natural language understanding (sentiment analysis, paraphrase detection, reading comprehension, NLI), reasoning (math/commonsense/ethical reasoning), knowledge-based QA, and text generation (code generation, summarization, data-to-text, semantic parsing). Not planning/agents/tool-use specific.
problem_setting: A survey (literature review) of retrieval-augmented in-context learning. The reviewed setting: given a test query q* and a retrieval corpus C of candidate demonstrations d_i=(q_i,a_i), a demonstration retriever DR selects a set {d_1,...,d_k} from C to prepend to q* so the frozen LLM maximizes the probability of the correct answer a*. The LLM parameters are not fine-tuned (training-free adaptation); only the (optional) retriever is trained. Single-model, offline-corpus setting (retrieval corpus is typically a static labeled training set, in-domain / mix-domain / cross-domain / unlabelled-with-generated-answers / free-form). The survey organizes the design space along three axes: retrieval models (off-the-shelf vs fine-tuned retrievers), retriever training procedures (training-data collection + objectives), and inference algorithms (one-shot / clustering / iterative retrieval). It is not interactive/agentic and not multi-agent.
what_is_retrieved: demos / ICL demonstrations: input-output exemplars d_i=(q_i,a_i) (e.g. (query, label) or (question, answer/reasoning chain)) tailored per query. The survey is exclusively about retrieving few-shot demonstrations (not tools, docs-as-evidence, skills, or trajectories).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: the surveyed methods retrieve from a fixed demonstration corpus (most commonly a labeled training set, optionally a subset, mixed-task pool, cross-domain set, or free-form/unlabelled corpus with auto-generated answers). The survey notes that nearly all current work uses a static, constant retrieval corpus; it flags 'Active Demonstration Retrieval' (a growing corpus updated with new incoming queries) only as an open future direction, not as established practice.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Predominantly fixed top-k ranking, but the survey explicitly contrasts independent top-k selection with set-level composition. It distinguishes 'one-hoc' (one-shot) retrieval where each of the top-k demonstrations is chosen independently (risking homogeneity) versus clustering retrieval and iterative retrieval that aim for diversity/coverage and selecting demonstrations that complement each other (a set-composition / coverage objective). It also covers diversity objectives (e.g. DPP) that model negative interactions among selected demonstrations. The selection count k is still a fixed budget in practice.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (the survey is not framed as case-based reasoning; in CBR terms only the Retrieve phase is covered - demonstrations are retrieved and reused verbatim as ICL exemplars, with no Revise/Retain of cases).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the survey does not frame retrieval-based ICL as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is framed as demonstration retrieval / RetICL (retrieval models, training, inference algorithms).
retrieval_unit: single demonstration (one ICL exemplar = an input-output pair d_i=(q_i,a_i)); the retrieved object as a whole is a set of k such demonstrations. Demonstrations may include chain-of-thought reasoning chains where applicable, but the indexed/retrieved unit is the demonstration (snippet-level exemplar), not a trajectory, tool, or KG-subgraph.
index_source: Static corpus, built offline: the retrieval corpus is typically the task's labeled training set (in-domain IID), or a representative subset, or a combination of multiple tasks (mix-domain), or cross-domain annotated data, or unlabelled queries with LLM-auto-generated answers, or a free-form text corpus (e.g. Wikipedia for pseudo-demonstrations). Demonstrations are encoded and indexed once; the store is frozen at test time. Online/test-time-growing corpora are only discussed as a future direction (active demonstration retrieval).
index_structure_topology: Flat dense/sparse vector index: candidate demonstrations are encoded (BM25 term vectors, SBERT/sentence embeddings, or dual-encoder dense vectors) and retrieved by similarity (cosine / inner product / BM25 score). Clustering-retrieval methods add k-means sub-grouping over the embeddings (a shallow partition for diversity), but there is no graph or deep hierarchy. No knowledge-graph or dependency-graph index.
retriever_type: Surveys multiple types: (1) off-the-shelf - term-based sparse (BM25), sentence-embedding similarity (SBERT, RoBERTa, optionally NLI/STS-finetuned), and pretrained dual encoders (DPR-style); (2) fine-tuned learned dense retrievers (dual-encoder, contrastively/list-wise/distillation trained); plus optional cross-encoder rerankers. Covers heuristic/off-the-shelf, learned-dense, and learned-with-LM-feedback retrievers. Generative tool-as-token retrievers are out of scope.
retriever_learning_signal: Spans the full spectrum the survey organizes in Section 5: (a) none / off-the-shelf (BM25, SBERT, dual encoders used as-is); (b) LM-feedback supervision - a scoring LLM (ideally the inference LLM, often a smaller same-family proxy) scores candidates by s(d)=p(a|d,q); top/bottom ranked become positive/negative training pairs; (c) contrastive InfoNCE, list-wise ranking loss (LambdaRank-inspired), KL-divergence distillation from a cross-encoder/reward teacher, and multi-objective combinations; (d) model-free label-similarity heuristics (e.g. average F1 between query and demonstration labels); (e) iterative/RL training of the retriever (e.g. Scarlatos & Lan train an LSTM retriever with reinforcement learning; Lu et al. train an RL reranker). Iterative training mines harder negatives across rounds. Diversity training via Determinantal Point Processes (DPP).
query_construction: Primarily the raw test query is encoded as the search key. Variants surveyed: (i) one-shot - encode the raw query once and take top-k; (ii) clustering - query matched to one representative per cluster; (iii) iterative - the query is augmented with already-retrieved demonstration(s) before retrieving the next, so the effective query becomes history-conditioned. Some structural-similarity methods construct queries from the query's syntactic/reasoning structure. For unlabelled/free-form corpora, pseudo-demonstrations or LLM-generated answers may be created first.
query_granularity: Mostly task/query-level (one-shot retrieval at inference using the input query). Iterative-retrieval methods are step-level: a new query is formed at each of the k retrieval steps conditioned on previously selected demonstrations (a two-level / history-aware retrieval). Clustering retrieval is also query-level but enforces per-cluster selection.
when_to_retrieve: Survey covers one-shot (top-k in a single pass; the dominant 'one-hoc' strategy), clustering (single-pass but cluster-constrained), and iterative (k sequential retrieval steps conditioned on prior selections). Active/uncertainty-triggered retrieval and continually-updated corpora are discussed only as future directions, not as established practice.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule in the reviewed methods: retrieval is performed once (one-shot) or for a predetermined number of iterations to assemble k demonstrations; the trigger is the need for the few-shot prompt, not a learned/confidence-based signal. The survey identifies learned/active triggering (selecting which new examples to annotate-and-add as input distribution shifts, akin to active learning) as an explicitly open future direction ('Active Demonstration Retrieval').
reranking: Yes - the survey reviews a two-stage retriever-reranker architecture (Section 5.2 'Re-ranker Training'): a fast dual-encoder retriever first selects top-N candidates, then a slower cross-encoder reranker (capturing token-level interactions) reranks them and the top-K are used to build the prompt. Reranker training uses sigmoid cross-entropy; one variant (Lu et al.) trains the reranker via reinforcement learning. Reranking is presented as an optional enhancement, not universal.
retrieved_context_refinement: Mostly none - retrieved demonstrations are inserted into the prompt as exemplars. The main post-retrieval operations the survey discusses are (a) reranking (cross-encoder two-stage) and (b) set-level diversity selection (clustering / DPP) to reduce homogeneity/redundancy. There is no decompose-then-recompose, reason-in-documents distillation, or compression of demonstration content; demonstrations are used in raw exemplar form.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/skills; demonstrations are raw input-output text pairs encoded by the retriever. For free-form/unlabelled corpora, pseudo-labels or LLM-generated answers may be attached to candidate text before indexing, but this is corpus construction, not tool-description engineering.)
index_content_separation: N/A - a demonstration is both the indexed unit (via its embedding) and the content injected into the prompt; no lightweight-index-then-heavy-content (progressive-disclosure) separation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool APIs / live tool stores; the corpus is a static demonstration pool. Continually-updated corpora are only a future direction.)
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependencies; demonstrations are independent exemplars, though clustering/DPP model inter-demonstration redundancy/diversity rather than dependency.)
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: the selected k demonstrations are concatenated before the test query as the few-shot ICL context (d_1,...,d_k,q*) and fed to the frozen LLM, whose parameters are unchanged. Retrieved demonstrations also serve as a training signal in the retriever-training pipeline (a scoring LLM's p(a|d,q) labels which demonstrations are positive/negative for retriever learning). No case adaptation or latent-token injection.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-generate (one-shot exemplars at inference time): demonstrations are retrieved and assembled into a single ICL prompt before one LLM generation; there is no planning, MCTS/tree-search, or per-step interleaving with the LLM's reasoning. Iterative-retrieval methods run a retrieval-side loop to compose the demonstration set, but the LLM still performs a single answer generation afterward. (RetICL is orthogonal to agent planning.)
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer: the retrieval (whether one-shot or k-step iterative composition) happens before a single LLM answer/generation. Retrieval is not woven into per-CoT-step, per-token, or per-tool-call reasoning of the LLM; the iterative steps, when present, are over demonstration selection, not over the LLM's reasoning trace.
adaptation_mechanism: verbatim ICL exemplar - retrieved demonstrations are used as-is in the prompt; the survey does not cover LLM-prompted or feedback-driven revision of retrieved demonstrations (no CBR-style case adaptation).
retrieved_item_representation: raw demonstration (a natural-language input paired with its output/label, optionally including a chain-of-thought reasoning chain), injected as a verbatim few-shot example in the prompt. No distillation into strategies/guidelines, workflows, programs, or latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: single demonstration (raw input-output exemplar), the lowest abstraction level. The survey does not retrieve distilled strategies, workflows, skills, or guideline-rules; CoT-augmented demonstrations are still concrete exemplars, not abstracted insights.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Mainly retriever-training-based and set-diversity-based: training the retriever on LM-feedback signals (positive demonstrations raise p(a|d,q), negatives mislead it) so it learns to avoid unhelpful exemplars; contrastive/list-wise objectives with hard-negative mining (and iterative training to mine better negatives); two-stage reranking to filter top-N down to high-quality top-K; clustering/DPP diversity to avoid homogeneous/redundant demonstrations. The survey also notes a robustness finding: retrieved demonstrations can HARM commonsense-reasoning and coreference tasks (random can be better), a cautionary noise observation. No explicit self-reflection or reason-in-documents distillation module.
memory_type: none - no episodic/skill/workflow memory; the only persistent store is the static demonstration corpus (the labeled training set). No growing memory is maintained by the reviewed methods (active/growing corpora are a future direction only).
write_back: False - the surveyed RetICL methods do not write new experiences/cases/skills into memory during deployment; the retrieval corpus is fixed. (The survey raises corpus-growth/active demonstration retrieval as an open problem, not an implemented mechanism.)
online_growth: False - the retrieval corpus is static/frozen after offline construction in essentially all reviewed work; the survey explicitly notes 'Much of the current research is based on a static framework where the retrieval corpus remains constant' and proposes online corpus updating only as future work.
write_back_trigger: never (at deployment) for the reviewed methods - nothing is written to the corpus during/after inference. The survey's future-direction 'Active Demonstration Retrieval' would add a human-validated / annotation-gated write (select a representative subset of incoming unlabelled queries for annotation, then add to the corpus), but this is proposed, not realized.
failure_experience_usage: No persistent storage of failed experiences. However, in retriever TRAINING the survey describes using both positive (LLM-helpful) and negative (LLM-misleading) demonstrations contrastively (InfoNCE / list-wise / hard-negative mining), so 'failure' signals inform retriever training - but failures are not stored as retrievable corrective items at inference. Success-only at deployment.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / none - no deployed memory to mutate (static corpus). Iterative retriever TRAINING re-mines positives/negatives across rounds (a training-time refinement of the retriever, not a mutation of stored memory entries).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially / surveyed as one option: most reviewed methods use fixed similarity-based top-k or contrastively-trained dense retrievers (not RL policies), but the survey explicitly covers learned-policy / RL approaches for iterative retrieval (Scarlatos & Lan's LSTM retriever trained with reinforcement learning) and an RL-trained reranker (Lu et al.). So retrieval-as-learned-policy is included in the taxonomy but is not the dominant paradigm.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No - single-model demonstration retrieval; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing. The survey does note transferability across inference LLMs (a retriever trained with one scoring LLM can serve a different/larger inference LLM, since smaller same-family scorers are often used for labeling), i.e. cross-model retriever reuse, but not multi-agent sharing.
benchmarks: As a survey it catalogs datasets used across the reviewed RetICL literature rather than running its own. Examples cited by application category: NLU - SST/SST-5 (sentiment), MRPC/PAWS (paraphrase), SQuAD/BoolQ/OpenBookQA (reading comprehension), MNLI/SNLI/RTE/CB (NLI); Reasoning - GSM8K/MathQA/AQuA (math), CommonsenseQA (CMSQA)/HellaSwag/PIQA/COPA (commonsense), ethical-reasoning sets; Knowledge-based QA - WebQuestions, Natural Questions, TriviaQA, ARC; Text generation - code generation (GeoQuery/semantic parsing), summarization, data-to-text. (Specific dataset-to-method pairings are in Section 6 and the appendix tables.)
benchmark_family: QA (open-domain and knowledge-based QA), plus general NLU/GLUE-style classification, reasoning (math GSM8K-style; commonsense CommonsenseQA/HellaSwag), and text generation (code generation / semantic parsing). Not in the agentic web/embodied/tool/code-agent/memory-dialogue benchmark families; it predates and is orthogonal to ALFWorld/WebArena/ToolBench/SWE-bench/LoCoMo.
baselines: As comparison points within the surveyed design space: zero-shot, random few-shot, and fixed/manually-curated demonstrations as the lower-bound baselines; off-the-shelf retrievers (BM25, SBERT/sentence embeddings, pretrained dual encoders) vs fine-tuned/learned retrievers (EPR-style InfoNCE, list-wise/LambdaRank, DPP diversity, KL-distillation, iterative, RL). The survey contrasts off-the-shelf vs fine-tuned retrievers and one-shot vs clustering vs iterative inference rather than reporting a single head-to-head leaderboard.
key_metrics: Downstream task metrics of the reviewed work: accuracy / F1 (classification, NLI, commonsense), exact match and answer accuracy (QA, math reasoning), and generation metrics (e.g. exact match / execution accuracy for code-generation & semantic parsing, ROUGE/BLEU for summarization & data-to-text). The survey reports qualitative comparisons (e.g. retrieval vs random) rather than a unified metric. Retrieval-intrinsic metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are largely not the focus.
headline_result: Survey-level takeaway: retrieving query-tailored demonstrations substantially and consistently improves ICL over fixed/random demonstrations across most NLU, reasoning, QA, and generation tasks, and reduces sensitivity to demonstration ordering. A concrete cited number: Ye et al. (2023) report 10+% improvement on open-domain QA using BM25-retrieved demonstrations. An important caveat: on commonsense reasoning and coreference tasks, random demonstrations can outperform retrieval-based selection.
ablations: As a survey it aggregates findings rather than running ablations, but it synthesizes component-level evidence: (1) off-the-shelf vs fine-tuned retrievers - fine-tuned/learned retrievers generally outperform off-the-shelf ones by tailoring to the task, though off-the-shelf already beats random; (2) similarity vs diversity - diversity (clustering/DPP) matters notably for mathematical reasoning (Zhang et al. 2022), and DPP fine-tuning improves over pure similarity (Ye et al. 2023); (3) one-shot vs iterative - iterative retrieval gives the most significant gains on math reasoning (Scarlatos & Lan 2023); (4) scoring-LLM choice - using the inference LLM (or a smaller same-family proxy) as scorer best reflects its preferences; (5) corpus subset vs full - retrieving from a carefully selected representative subset can match retrieving from the full training set (Hongjin et al. 2022 vs Ye et al. 2023); (6) task-dependence - retrieval can hurt commonsense/coreference tasks.
evaluation_decoupling: Largely No / not standardized - the survey reports end-to-end downstream task metrics from the reviewed papers; it does not impose or systematically report decoupled intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) separated from task performance. It notes the limited understanding of WHY retrieved demonstrations help (calling for theory), implicitly highlighting the lack of decoupled retrieval-quality evaluation.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Outcome-focused: the reviewed evaluations score final task outputs (accuracy/EM/F1/generation metrics). Intermediate/process metrics (retrieval-step accuracy, reasoning faithfulness) are generally not reported; the survey itself flags the missing theoretical/process understanding of demonstration retrieval as an open problem.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively: RetICL improves efficiency and scalability of adaptation vs fine-tuning (no parameter updates) and vs manual example curation. The survey notes index efficiency tradeoffs - BM25/sparse retrievers are far more index- and memory-efficient (preferred with very large demonstration pools and limited hardware), while dense dual-encoders capture semantics but cost more; two-stage retriever-reranker trades extra reranking cost for quality; using a smaller same-family scoring LLM reduces labeling cost. No unified latency/API-cost numbers are tabulated. [uncertain on exact cost figures]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k demonstration budget in the reviewed methods: a retriever selects k demonstrations (one-shot top-k, one-per-cluster for k clusters, or k iterative steps). Two-stage methods retrieve top-N then rerank-and-truncate to top-K. The survey discusses k as a tunable budget and reviews work studying performance vs number of demonstrations, but k is generally fixed per experiment rather than adaptively/precision-driven. No explicit token-budget cap framework.
survey_scope_and_axes: Explicit organizing axes: (1) Retrieval-based ICL design choices - retrieval objectives (similarity vs diversity), inference/retrieval strategy (one-shot 'one-hoc' / clustering / iterative), and retrieval corpus (in-domain / mix-domain / cross-domain / unlabelled-with-generated-answers / free-form); (2) Off-the-shelf retrievers (term-based BM25 / sentence-embedding SBERT / pretrained dual encoder); (3) Fine-tuned retrievers - training-data collection (LLM-signal-based vs model-free) and training objectives (list-wise ranking / InfoNCE / KL-distillation / multi-objective / iterative / diversity-DPP / reranker); plus Applications and Future Directions. Reference count: 175 references (Semantic Scholar). Coverage window: ICL-with-retrieved-demonstrations literature through early 2024 (survey v5 March 2024).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark-construction paper; it surveys methods and aggregates existing datasets across reviewed works rather than building a new benchmark).
builds_on: Synthesizes and builds on the foundational RetICL line: KATE (Liu et al. 2022, semantic-similarity demonstration retrieval), EPR (Rubin et al. 2022, LM-scored InfoNCE-trained retriever), CEIL (Ye et al. 2023, DPP set selection), Li et al. 2023b (unified/list-wise demonstration retriever), Luo et al. 2023 (Dr.ICL / retriever training), Cheng et al. 2023; off-the-shelf encoders BM25 (Robertson), SBERT (Reimers & Gurevych), DPR/dual-encoder (Karpukhin et al.), and ICL foundations (Brown et al. 2020 GPT-3; Min et al. 2022). Builds on retrieval (DPR, Contriever) and ICL literature.
contrasts_with: Positioned against fixed/manually-curated and random-few-shot ICL (context-insensitive demonstrations), and against non-retrieval advanced selection by complexity/diversity/difficulty/perplexity that still selects a static set. Within RetICL it contrasts off-the-shelf vs fine-tuned retrievers, similarity-only vs diversity-aware selection, and one-shot independent top-k vs clustering/iterative set composition. As a survey it is distinguished from broader RAG / LLM-agent surveys by its narrow, dedicated focus on demonstration retrieval for ICL.
lineage: Surveys group; anchors Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval). It is the dedicated survey of retrieval-based in-context learning, organizing the lineage from off-the-shelf similarity retrieval (BM25/SBERT) -> LM-feedback-trained dense retrievers (KATE -> EPR -> CEIL -> list-wise/iterative/RL retrievers) and along the inference-strategy axis (one-shot -> clustering -> iterative). It serves as the taxonomic anchor for the demonstration-retrieval (Group A) sub-topic of the broader retrieval-augmented LLM agents survey.
